chapter: The Original Dixieland band to California
title: Back in Baton Rouge in 1926; Houston man seeking a band for Oakland
summary: Joe dates his return to Baton Rouge to 1926, when a Houston man recruited a Dixieland band for two Oakland backers.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Let me try to get this into some kind of order here with the dates. Now, after you left the circus and went back to Baton Rouge, around what year was that?
That had to be last... It had to be '26.
Well, that was about when I guess those Hot Five records were suddenly coming out.
That's right. Because when I come...
Okay, now we can pick up from where you were talking about Ory had just left Los Angeles.

Yeah. This guy comes through here looking for a band, a guy out of Houston, Texas, looking for a band to go to Oakland and San Francisco, named Toby Mitchell. He was representing two guys out of Oakland, a Jewish guy named Ben Bespawn(?) I think was his name, and another guy named Charlie Hill, I believe, who was a colored guy that had a restaurant in Oakland.

Well, these guys never amounted to nothin'. But they was trying to get a band together and to become managers of a band, because they thought they could make some money. Dixieland was just a coming thing at the time.
But what we're saying about the Hot Five records and things like that coming about at the same time... I guess the Hot Five records helped push that kind of music, didn't it?
Oh, yes. No question about it.
